thread:
maya: Hey — noticed intermittent 502/timeout from pods to our model-registry service through the interface endpoint in eu-west-1. Happens when scale > ~60 pods. No obvious app errors. Any networking guesses?
jon: Can you paste a curl + dig output from a failing pod and from a bastion in same AZ?
maya: from pod (inside cluster):
```
$ dig model-registry.internal +short
10.0.45.12
10.0.46.9

$ curl -v http://model-registry.internal/health
* Connected to 10.0.45.12 (10.0.45.12) port 80 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: model-registry.internal
> 
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
from bastion in same subnet:
```
$ dig model-registry.internal +short
10.0.45.12
10.0.45.13

$ curl -v http://model-registry.internal/health
* Connected to 10.0.45.13 (10.0.45.13) port 80 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: model-registry.internal
> 
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
jon: hmm pod and bastion resolve differently and pod hits 10.0.46.9 which is an ENI in a different subnet. Could be endpoint ENI placement + route mismatch.
infra-bot: Alert: subnet-a (10.0.46.0/24) ENI quota at 92% (47/51) — iface endpoint created additional ENIs this morning.
kai: FYI we enabled a conditional forwarder to on-prem resolver for *.internal last week (per infra/ldap migration). That could produce split-horizon DNS where pods use cluster DNS config and get forwarded answers that differ. Also if endpoint has EnablePrivateDnsName = true, it registers private DNS names onto endpoint ENIs.
nash (via DM to maya): check endpoint security group egress and whether it allows traffic from pod CIDR ephemeral ports. If endpoint SG only allows established flows from bastion, new pod ports might be dropped.
nash (public reply): Also check route tables attached to the subnets where endpoint ENIs are placed — if they point to a NAT GW (0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-xxx) and we're relying on internal routing to the service, traffic could be routed out and break connection tracking.
maya: confirmed endpoint SG had only outbound 443/80 to the registry SG, but no explicit allow from pod CIDR for ephemeral ports. Security team created stricter SGs last month.
jon: Steps I'd try: 1) temporarily disable the conditional forwarder so VPC DNS does not split-horizon; 2) verify EnablePrivateDnsName on the endpoint; 3) add pod CIDR to endpoint SG ingress/egress as needed; 4) if ENI placement causes over-allocation, move endpoint to subnets with room or increase ENI limits.
kai: we tried disabling resolver rule in staging — pods then resolved to same two IPs as bastion and requests succeeded. So that points to DNS split + endpoint ENI in a subnet with different route table/NAT behavior.
nash: created quick fix: added pod CIDR (10.0.40.0/22) to endpoint SG egress, and temporarily turned off the conditional forwarder rule.
maya: applying change now to prod canary (5 pods)
maya: canary ok for 12m, no 502s. Scaling to 80 to reproduce — still stable.
jon: sounds like two root causes: conditional forwarder created inconsistent resolution and endpoint SG + ENI placement exposed packets to a route that caused SNAT/fallback. Both fixed.
kai: follow-up: we should update runbook: when creating interface endpoints, always ensure: EnablePrivateDnsName set appropriately, resolver rules checked for overlap, endpoint SG allows pod CIDR ephemeral ports, and pick subnets with ENI capacity.
maya: agreed. I'll open a quick RFC to make endpoint creation checklist. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident closed (inc-2026-03-epe-dns-nat)
summary: Intermittent 502s to internal model-registry via interface endpoint caused by split-horizon DNS (conditional forwarder) plus endpoint security group/ENI placement issues. Resolved by disabling resolver rule and adding pod CIDR to endpoint SG; canary validated.
